title: fix(plugin-grid,app-shell): a CSV file reaches the import door as CSV text
body:
Fixes #13315
Clause-②: no

**Build PR, on the maintainer's ruling A** (the option labelled 「A 重写成 CSV 发送 (Recommended)」, recorded on objectui#13315 in comment 6328933548). A CSV file source now reaches the server's CSV import door: the import wizard sends `format: 'csv'` with `sourceRowsToCsv(rows)`, the cells the preview parsed. The identity import's adapter takes the same change. Neither parser changes: `parseDelimited` is byte-identical, and objectstack's `parseCsvToRows` is not touched.

Dispatched by objectstack `domain:cli` seat 2 on objectui#13315's claim (comment 6327882289), session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01AFrKwndmrCLtF5V9hNtrw3`. The disclosure ruling on objectstack-ai/objectstack#9387 applies: this PR describes the change at the card's level only.

## What changed

- **The request (`assembleImportRequest`, `ImportWizard.tsx`).** A new `csvFile` option. With it, the hand-mapped path sends `{ format: 'csv', csv: sourceRowsToCsv(rows) }`, and a named mapping sends CSV text unless it declares `sourceFormat: 'json'`, which the door refuses CSV for (`MAPPING_FORMAT_MISMATCH`). A `csv`-declared mapping sends CSV text from any source, as before (#13156). An .xlsx sheet and a paste keep JSON rows. The dry-run pre-check, the background job and the sync import all send the one request `buildImportRequest` assembles.
- **What carries "this is a CSV file" (H1).** `assembleImportRequest` cannot see the source, and no new prop was needed. The wizard keeps one boolean state, `csvFile`, set where the grid is loaded: the upload step's file path and the `initialFile` effect answer `delimitedFileDelimiter(file.name) !== null`, a paste answers false, and reset clears it. `delimitedFileDelimiter` (`importParsers.ts`) is the name test `parseSpreadsheetFile` already picked its text arm with, moved into a named function that both now read, so "a CSV file" means the same thing to the parse and to the request: `.csv`, `.tsv` and `.txt`, the delimited-text inputs the card's item 2 measured as CSV. `parseSpreadsheetFile` behaves exactly as before.
- **The identity import (`identityImport.ts`, H2).** The adapter batched the request's `rows`, and a CSV request has none, so it would have thrown. `batchIdentityImportRequest` now cuts a CSV request at record boundaries (`readCsvRequestRecords`): each batch of at most 500 rows is posted as the header record plus its data records, joined by CRLF, which for the wizard's text is exactly `sourceRowsToCsv` of that batch's rows. Each batch's rows are read from the same records, so the one-time-password reveal still names every row by its email or phone. JSON rows are batched as before.

Why the adapter reads the wizard's text back instead of receiving rows: the wizard calls one `importRecords(object, request)` for every data source and cannot tell the identity adapter from the generic one, which posts the request as it is. Carrying the rows beside the text would double the generic door's payload, and a new parameter on `DataSource.importRecords` would widen a published interface. The scan splits records the way the door's CSV parse does, keeps each record's bytes as written, and decides no imported value.

## Measured (H2, H3)

- **H2, numbering across batches.** A one-shot script ran the adapter's batching on a 1203-line file (a quoted comma, a quoted LF, a quoted CRLF, doubled quotes, an export-marked cell, a blank line, and rows whose mapped cells are all empty at preview rows 250 and 500), then objectstack's `parseCsvToRows` on every batch body, at `main` `abc25a3536` and at objectstack-ai/objectstack#25130's head `bf8244cb20` (read from git objects, transpiled unchanged). Both refs read the same: every batch body equals `sourceRowsToCsv` of that batch's rows, the adapter's rows equal the preview's rows, and 0 server rows differ from the preview row at the same renumbered index. One preview row is never read: row 500, the last of batch 1, whose mapped cells are all empty. That is B1 at a batch end; sent as one request, the file keeps it. So numbering stays aligned, and in the identity import B1 holds for the last row of every batch, not only the file's last. The changeset says so.
- **H3, a marked header.** On the default path the text is headed by field names, so a header the export marked (`'=Region`, auto-mapped to `region`) reaches the server as `region`. Pinned.

## Pins

`ImportWizard.csvFileSource-13315.test.tsx` drives the real wizard to its real request. A `.csv` file on the default path sends `format: 'csv'` with the corrected preview cells, and the dry run sends the same payload. A `.tsv` or `.txt` file picked in the upload step is a CSV file too. A marked header still maps. An undeclared named mapping sends CSV text with `mappingName`. CONTROLS: a `json`-declared mapping, an .xlsx sheet and a paste send JSON rows.

`identityImport.csvBatches-13315.test.tsx` covers the batching itself (quoted commas, a quoted line break, doubled quotes, an all-empty row, a header alone refused before any request, JSON rows batched as JSON). It also runs the real wizard and the real adapter on a 1001-row `.csv` file: three CSV batches cut from the wizard's text, results renumbered 1 to 1001, and a one-time password on row 777 named `user777@example.test`. CONTROL: a paste goes out as JSON rows.

`ImportWizard.csvDoorParity-13315.test.tsx`, the measurement test, now pins the shipped route: its B1 case drives the real wizard and asserts the CSV request. Its FILE TEXT cases and its recorded B2 and B3 rows stay, as the record of why the file's own text was not sent and of the shapes the route was accepted with.

Ablation, one-shot, with objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` on the committed head `ba5cc54`; each mutation was proven on disk and restored to the HEAD blob:
- A, the hand-mapped arm ignores `csvFile`: 6 red (the .csv, .tsv, .txt and marked-header pins, the parity B1 case, the 1001-row identity case), 16 green.
- B, the identity adapter ignores a CSV request: 2 red (the batching case and the 1001-row case), 4 green.

## The shapes the changeset states (B1 to B3)

Stated at user level, per the disclosure ruling. A last row whose mapped cells are all empty is not imported; in the identity import, the same holds for the last row of each 500-row batch. A cell that begins with an apostrophe, continues with `+` or `-`, holds only digits, spaces and `( ) + - . ,` and ends in a tab or a line break keeps the apostrophe, as it did before. A space before a leading apostrophe is trimmed first, so such a cell now imports without the apostrophe.

## Acceptance notes

Observations, not filed and not fixed here:
- `parseDelimited`'s doc comment says trailing whitespace is trimmed, but the code trims both ends of every cell, and B3 rests on the leading half. Not fixed, because the ruling leaves both parsers unchanged. Carrier: none.
- Once objectstack-ai/objectstack#25130 lands, the preview still checks cells as the file spells them (`checkImportCell`), and matches a named mapping's columns by the header as written (`savedMappingToDisplayIndexMap`). So a marked select value or a marked header shows as a preview finding or an unmatched column, while the server accepts it. Dormant until that PR lands. Carrier: none.
- objectstack's `parseCsvToRows`, read as a function only: a leading blank line becomes the header row, an inner blank line becomes a row, and a repeated header keeps the last column, while its doc comment says the first non-empty line is the header. Not reached from here: this PR never sends the file's own text. Carrier: none.
